setting: Hill farm, Co. Mayo, lambing, 2 a.m., rain. We are in the farmhouse kitchen: May's handheld is on the table.

GERRY.name: Cillian
GERRY.note: farmer, 40s; hay shed, then yard, then the lambing shed

MAY.name: Clare - Soft and Warm (West of Ireland)
MAY.note: his wife, in the kitchen with us: room voice, red light

JO.name: Michelle - Direct and Natural
JO.note: 60s, farms on her own across the valley

lines.text: —ill in the hay shed with the lame one. Her foot's in a terrible state. I'll do the lambing shed after this.
lines.say: Still in the hay shed with the lame one. Her foot's in a terrible state. I'll do the lambing shed after this.

lines.text: Ah, grand. This one's taking the bottle now. Bit of fight in her.
That you two still up? I've had three since midnight, and all of them backwards.
Go to bed, Jo.
Go to bed yourself.
Ah, for God's sake. Would you listen to them. Something's got in with the ewes.
Jo, if that's your bloody dog again, I swear to God.
Both my dogs are in. They're lying here by the fire.
Well, something's in there. I'm going down.
A fox?
If it's a fox, it's a dead fox.
May. They've gone quiet.
Can you see it?
No. Sixty ewes and not a sound. They're all stood facing the back corner. Every one of them. Same corner.
Gerry. Come out of there.
It's a fox, Jo. I've got the torch.
Right. I'm at the back pen. There's—
It's not a fox.
Gerry? ... Gerry, what is it?
May. His shed lights have gone. I can see your place from here. The whole shed's gone dark.
Gerry, answer me.
May.
I'm here. What's in the corner?
May.
May, there's someone crossing your yard. Under the light. Coming up to the house.
Gerry, is that you?

notes.ending: After l26 nothing on the radio; the lamb stops; three slow knocks on the back door, in the room; cut.
notes.calm: l22 and l24 are the same calm 'May.' with the tin roof behind: he is still in the shed when the knocks come.
notes.clip: PTT clip only on lines whose first word can be lost; it turned 'May' into 'Hey' and 'Gerry' into 'Sherry'.
